relevance_note: Single-patient case report of HA20: "Whole exome sequencing identified a heterozygous de novo pathogenic variant of the TNFAIP3 gene (c. 1777 C>T in exon 7, p.Q593X)" in a child with a lupus-like phenotype.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown file by hand; it contains no data tables and no supplementary section, so no table was transcribed by script and no stacked-cell (' / ') situation arose. Scope: the single patient (rule 5 label 'patient') plus the two parents, who are in scope as relatives tested for the variant ("neither parent harbors the p.Q593X pathogenic variant") and who are labelled by relation only, since the paper says only 'both parents'/'neither parent' and never gives their sex. Excluded from rows, with reasons: (a) the patient's maternal and paternal grandmothers, mentioned only to document parental consanguinity ("the patient's maternal grandmother and paternal grandmother were sisters"); they are neither tested nor reported affected and are not described in relation to a TNFAIP3 variant or HA20 diagnosis, so they were treated as out of scope; (b) the 3 patients of Yu et al.'s review ("3 patients, two of whom had prominent mucosal ulcer involvement and the third with an eventual diagnosis of both autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) and HA20") - the mucosal ulceration is a count that names no individual, and the third person has no individual-level fact beyond the diagnosis, so none of the three is an identifiable in-scope person; (c) the patients of the Aeschlimann (16 patients), CVID (12) and ALPS (13) cohorts, mentioned only as counts; (d) the p.Q593X findings in a MALT lymphoma and a basal cell carcinoma, which the paper says were somatic ("both of these mutations were somatic (identified in the tumor cells)"). Judgement calls recorded: oral ulcers were set 'excluded' because the paper states for this individual that "mucosal ulcers have not been a feature of our patient's clinical course at any point in her life"; genital ulcers were left 'not reported' because the paper does not address them separately. Central nervous system involvement was left 'not reported': the paper reports concern for meningitis, headache and elevated CSF white cells but never states CNS involvement, and the infectious work-up was negative. Variant type 'nonsense' was recorded from the paper's own statement that the change "results in a premature stop codon"; the paper does not use the word 'nonsense'. No functional assay was performed ("biochemical studies have not been performed"), so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Time-dependent rather than contradictory findings, noted because the same item is both normal and abnormal at different ages: complement ("normal complement C3 and C4 levels" at 7.5 years vs "suppressed C3, C4, and CH50" at 8-11 years, and "normal or elevated" at 12-14 years) and immunoglobulins ("normal to elevated" at 7.5 years vs progressive hypogammaglobulinemia later); both are recorded as separate phenotypic_features rows with their own spans. Negative findings were recorded per D-27 for the abnormalities they name; some minor negatives (e.g. EBER-ISH negative, normal B-cell counts) were not recorded. The paper states that its HA20 diagnosis is "presumptive and not confirmed".

study_type.span: Case Report: A Novel TNFAIP3 Mutation Causing Haploinsufficiency of A20 With a Lupus-Like Phenotype

n_patients_reported.span: We have identified a novel mutation in the gene encoding A20 in a pediatric patient with chronic lymphadenopathy, lupus-like symptoms, and progressive hypogammaglobulinemia.

cites_prior_report_of_same_patients.span: Our patient’s specific p.Q593X A20 mutation has previously been reported in a MALT lymphoma (14) as well as a basal cell carcinoma (15) though both of these mutations were somatic (identified in the tumor cells) whereas our patient’s p.Q593X mutation is germline.

Her fevers and neutropenia resolved after receiving broad spectrum antibiotics and discontinuing the MMF.
